newsitem.title: USA: Kellogg, Quaker watching General Mills price hike.
newsitem.headline: Kellogg, Quaker watching General Mills price hike.

text.p: Major U.S. ready-to-eat cereal makers are taking a wait-and-see stance on a decision by General Mills Inc Wednesday to increase cereal prices by an average of 2.6 percent.
"We will watch the category," said Mark Dollins, spokesman for Quaker Oats Co. "We are a smaller player in the category."

Quaker Oats, whose cereals include Life and Cap'n Crunch, had cut cereal prices an average of 15 percent in April last year. For the January through March period this year, Quaker Oats cereal volumes rose 27 percent over same period last year, he noted.
Meanwhile, Kellogg Co, the largest cereal maker in the U.S., declined comment on General Mills plans.
"We wouldn't comment on future business plans," said Kellogg spokesman Anthony Hebron. "We have said and continue to be optimistic about the long term growth of the business," he said.
He added that Kellogg has not increased cereal prices since 1994 and in April last year reduced prices an average of 19 percent.

Officials of Post Cereal, a unit of Philip Morris Cos Inc's Kraft Foods Inc, were not immediately available to comment on the action by General Mills, the second largest cereal maker in the U.S.. More than a year ago, Post had cut cereal prices by 20 percent triggering some selective reductions by competitors.
